findings.title: The black-hole edits the jury asked for are missing from both refined images, so the model lacks them too. Painted one colour, it reads as a camera with a protruding lens hood.
findings.evidence: The jury and the refine prompts asked for: a deep well about 15 mm deep, one knife-edge lip, a tube coiling 1.5 turns into the well, tubes thinning over the top, and blocks leaning toward the lens. g_to3d and g_hero contain none of these, and the GLB follows the images. I measured a front depth profile myself and it matches the orchestrator's numbers. The rim is a soft rounded torus at r 23-28 mm, about 6 mm wide and sitting 0-5 mm deep. The glass is only 9.4-10.4 mm behind the rim. The hood sticks out about 25 mm from the body front: depth reaches 25 mm at r 33-45. Tube thickness is constant. The sketch's light photon ring around the lens has become a black hood. That change was the jury's choice (c_gravity_well), not a reconstruction error. Without the black/grey contrast, the remaining form signal is a convex outward hood plus a narrow dark slot (2 mm wide, 16.7 mm deep at r 20-22). This weakens criterion 1 (concept word to form) for the painted model. The textured digital model and the hero image still carry it through colour.
findings.fix: Either accept this and argue the concept through CMF in the hero image, or edit the print mesh before printing. Options: cut a conical well into the hood face, sharpen the rim to one crisp lip, and/or sculpt one tube spiralling into the rim. Then check the result with a one-colour greyscale render.

findings.title: The hidden right (dial) side is a mirror copy of the grip side: a second USB-C port and a second viewfinder eyepiece, and none on the back
findings.evidence: I made my own az180 and az215 renders and a height-relief map of the -z face (fidelity/hidden.jpg and right_relief.png). Both show a second recessed inset panel with a USB-C slot of the same geometry. The real port on the grip side measures about 4 x 8.3 mm outer, recessed about 1 mm, with an inner slot about 1 x 6 mm that goes about 0.9 mm deeper. The viewfinder block also has an eyepiece window on both side faces, and its back face is blank. The eyepiece facing sideways comes from g_to3d itself; the duplicate does not. These are real geometry, not texture, and they survive in the print STL. After one-colour paint, the jury will see two USB-C ports and a viewfinder that cannot be looked through from behind.
findings.fix: In the print STL, fill the duplicate port and the inset-panel step on the dial side (sculpt or a boolean fill, or filler and sanding after printing). Move the eyepiece recess to the back face of the viewfinder, or at least remove the duplicate.

findings.title: The PBR material maps make the painted shell metallic, which contradicts the matte/satin CMF
findings.evidence: I sampled the metallicRoughness texture at 6M surface points (B = metallic, G = roughness). Grey shell and tubes: metallic median 0.98 (p10 0.95), roughness 0.78. Black parts: metallic median 0.65 (p10-p90 0.00-0.75). Glass: metallic 0.05, roughness 0.10. Both g_to3d and g_hero specify matte or satin painted surfaces. The orchestrator's own renders ignore PBR, so the problem does not show there. Any PBR hero render from the GLB (Blender, KeyShot, three.js) will turn the grey into rough aluminium and the black into semi-metal.
findings.fix: Before the hero CMF render, override the materials: metallic 0 everywhere except deliberate metal accents. Grey roughness about 0.4-0.5 (satin pearl), body black about 0.85, glass as its own material. Or rebake the textures.

findings.title: Lens: the knurled ring is baked as a silver ring, the inner stepped rings are merged, and the glass is small
findings.evidence: Base-colour albedo is about 0.5 (light grey) at r 16-19 mm on the barrel lip and on the knurl band. g_to3d and g_hero both show a black knurled ring there, with only thin highlights. The tex sheet and the Tripo preview show it as a bright silver ring. The many concentric inner barrel rings in g_to3d became one smooth cone (r 9-13 mm). The glass is about 17 mm across inside a 40 mm barrel at 120 mm width (ratio 0.43), against about 0.5 in g_to3d and 38/50 in the prompt. So the 30 mm lens requirement holds only if the barrel (40 mm) or the hood opening (about 46-50 mm) counts as the lens, not the glass.
findings.fix: Paint the ring black in the base-colour texture, or give it its own material, for the CMF render. If the jury reads the lens size requirement strictly as the glass, enlarge the glass recess in the mesh. Scaling up does not help much: you would need about 1.7x (about 205 mm width).

findings.title: The tube crossing is partly merged: the crossing tube ends in a blunt stub and the S-tubes fuse into a flat band near the grip
findings.evidence: My close-up clay render at az110, el40 (fidelity/cross_clay.png) and the top view show the following. Three tubes leave the viewfinder face, matching g_to3d. But the front-right tube rises to a rounded dead end, with a hard crease seam along it, that butts against the third tube; it does not pass over it. In g_to3d it reads as a continuous tube crossing the braid; its upper end was hidden behind the dial block, so Tripo had to guess. Near the grip, the two S-tubes melt into one wide band with only a faint crease, where g_to3d shows two separate round tubes. The sketch's clear X-crossing is therefore less readable.
findings.fix: Optional sculpt: continue the stub over or behind the third tube, and deepen the valley between the S-tubes near the grip. Sand the crease seam on the printed part.

findings.title: Texture smudges and bleed on hidden or low-visibility areas
findings.evidence: Visible problems: faint vertical brush streaks on the grip front; dark smudges on the grey shoulder on the dial side (m_hero_tex_back34.png); black gradient bleeding across the bottom; a grey viewfinder neck where g_to3d shows black; a light halo ring at the shutter base. The orchestrator's renders are clean otherwise. The dark speckle in my own renders is an artefact of my point-splat renderer, not the texture.
findings.fix: Ignore for the painted print. For a hero render from the GLB, use flat procedural materials instead of the baked albedo, or touch up the texture.

findings.title: Hero CMF details are not in the model (titanium shutter and dial cap face)
findings.evidence: g_hero shows a titanium shutter cap and a titanium face on the dial cap. g_to3d and the GLB have black ones. The hero image and the digital or physical model will differ in these accents.
findings.fix: Assign a titanium material to the shutter and dial cap in the 3D hero render, or state that the hero image shows the CMF intent.

findings.title: Slight asymmetry: the hood rim plane tilts toward the grip side
findings.evidence: Rim depth around the circumference goes from 0 mm on the dial side to about 5 mm on the grip side across a rim diameter of about 52 mm, a tilt of about 5.5 degrees. Rim radius is a steady 25-27 mm and roughly concentric with the glass. This reads as a gentle lean and is not a defect.
findings.fix: No action needed. If the lean should support the 'pull' idea, mention it as intentional.

results.summary: Fidelity is good overall. The GLB's silhouette matches g_to3d at the best-fit view (az60, el18, IoU 0.95). Every visible feature is present as real geometry: hood with recessed glass, knurled barrel, shutter boss, recessed USB-C, viewfinder with eyepiece, knurled dial, three tubes plus the crossing tube. The bottom is flat to within 0.2 mm, so the model stands upright. The main deviations are: (1) the hidden dial side copies the grip side, so there is a second USB-C port and a second eyepiece; (2) the PBR maps make the grey and black surfaces metallic, and the lens ring is baked silver, so the hero CMF render needs material overrides; (3) the jury's well, coil and knife-edge edits never reached the refined images, so after one-colour paint the black-hole idea reads only as a protruding hood. None of these makes a deliverable or the print fail. Fixing (1) and overriding materials for (2) is recommended, and (3) is a design decision. My scratch renders are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-formnerd/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/scratchpad/verify/fidelity/: side_by_side.jpg, sil_diff.png, hidden.jpg, right_relief.png, cross_clay.png.

findings.title: >=30 mm lens requirement is met by the barrel, not by the glass
findings.evidence: I fitted the lens axis on a ray-cast front depth map and got y=65.09, z=32.13; frontmost x=90.17. Sections through the axis show these diameters. Glass dome: ~18 mm (edge crease at r≈9, 9.4-10.4 mm deep). Conical retaining bezel: opens to ~27 mm (r 13.5). Barrel front face: r 13.5-17 at 4.5 mm deep. Raised lip ring: r 17.2-18.5, so ~37 mm OD, 2 mm tall, 2.5 mm deep. Barrel outer wall: r 19.5-20.1, so OD ≈ 39-40 mm, running 12-14 mm back to the groove floor at x≈73.4. Funnel lip: inner r 22-23, crest r≈26-27 (Ø≈53 mm), blending into the body at r≈29-33. The funnel crest is tilted about 6° in yaw: its depth varies 0-5.6 mm around the ring. So the barrel (~39.5 mm), the lip ring (~37 mm) and the funnel (~53 mm) all clear 30 mm. The glass (18 mm) and the bezel opening (27 mm) do not. The orchestrator's profile is confirmed apart from two small corrections: the lip is r 17.2-18.5, not 17-20, and the groove is 2.3-3.0 mm wide, not 2. The barrel stays >=30 mm only if the print is at least ~92 mm wide (30/39.5 × 120).
findings.fix: In the deliverable, state that the lens (objektiv) is the Ø40 mm barrel inside the Ø53 mm funnel, and do not quote the glass diameter. Keep the print at >=92 mm width. If the jury is expected to read 'lens' as the glass, the glass/bezel has to be enlarged in CAD. Rescaling the whole model would need ~200 mm width, which is not realistic.

findings.title: Print lens-up (back/viewfinder on the plate), not upright as exported
findings.evidence: Overhangs >45° are similar in every orientation: 73.5 cm2 upright, 69.1 cm2 lens-up, 63.7 and 67.3 cm2 on either side, 94.0 cm2 upside down. What differs is where the support has to go. I cast rays down from each overhang to find what the support would land on. Upright (Z-up STL): 22.2 cm2 (projected) of support lands on the model, and 9.1 cm2 of that sits in gaps under 3 mm. This includes the 2.3-3 mm lens groove (2672 of 12383 tight samples) and the 4-7 mm tunnels under the tube bundle. Also, the barrel's underside is a 14 mm horizontal cantilever above the groove. Lens-up (+x up): only 2.6 cm2 lands on the model, 1.4 cm2 in tight gaps, and essentially none in the groove (18 samples), so the barrel, groove and lip all print as clean concentric vertical walls. The cost is plate contact. The viewfinder back sticks out 6.4 mm behind the main back panel, so only that face touches the plate (684 mm2, 38×18 mm). The back panel then needs ~60 cm2 of support from the plate. The two side-down orientations still trap support in the groove and make the part 120 mm tall.
findings.fix: Put +x up, standing on the viewfinder back. Use tree supports set to build plate only, plus a 5-8 mm brim. Use variable layer height (0.08-0.12 mm) over the top ~20 mm, which is the lens dome, bezel cone and lip. Sand the flat back panel after removing supports, which is easy. If the team still prints upright, set build-plate-only supports and accept some droop on the barrel underside and the groove ceiling.

findings.title: Lens groove is printable but cannot be sanded or filled
findings.evidence: Measured on x-slices, the groove runs between the barrel wall (r 19.5-20.1) and the funnel inner wall (r 22.0-23.1). It is 2.3 mm wide at the floor and 2.5-3.0 mm (median 2.6-3.4 mm) higher up, with a V-notch at x≈76 that widens to 3.6 mm. The floor is at x≈73.4. That is 12 mm below the barrel face, 14 mm below the lip and 16.8 mm below the frontmost point. STL and GLB slices agree to within ~0.05 mm.
findings.fix: No geometry change is needed for a 0.4 mm nozzle. Print it lens-up so no support ends up inside. Paint with thin spray coats and no filler primer, so paint does not pool in the slot. The dark slot reads as a shadow ring, which suits the black-hole concept.

findings.title: Sub-nozzle surface details will vanish under FDM and paint; the hard-requirement features survive
findings.evidence: I found thin and narrow regions by morphological opening on a 0.25 mm voxel grid (voxel volume 499.35 cm3, matching the mesh). Thinner than 1 mm: 117 mm3 in total. Most of it is the top of the lip ring, which is 1.1-1.5 mm wide and 2 mm tall. The rest is 0.25-0.5 mm step rings on the bezel at x≈85.6 and knurl texture under 0.5 mm on the dial cap and the lip top. Air gaps under 1 mm: the slit around the dial cap (Ø22, z≈80), the slit at the base of the shutter button, the <1 mm undercut notch on the barrel lip, and the panel seam around the back at z≈7. Under ~1 mm deep: recessed side panels on the viewfinder. The requirement features are large enough. The shutter button (top, x≈36-53, y≈13) is Ø≈16.5 mm and stands 2-5 mm proud. There is a USB-C recess on both sides (y=0 and y=120, centred at x≈26.5, z≈26): 3.5×8.5 mm outer, 1.5-1.9 mm deep, with an inner slot of ~2.3×6.4 mm deeper than 1 mm.
findings.fix: Accept that the knurl and micro-steps will be lost. Do not sand the lip ring, which is fragile at 1.1-1.5 mm. Mask or lightly re-scribe the shutter-button and dial-cap separation lines after priming so they still read. Keep the USB-C recess free of filler.

findings.title: Wedge crevices and small tunnels where the tubes meet the body
findings.evidence: The mesh has genus 7 (Euler number -12, one component), so there are 7 through-holes or handles. Air regions narrower than 1 mm add up to ~360 mm3. Most are wedge crevices where the tube bundle touches the body and where tubes touch each other (x 25-60, y 50-90, z 55-80). One example is a wedge tunnel 0.5-4 mm tall under the tubes at x=55, y 62-79, z 56-63. Upright, these are the main places where support would sit on the model (gaps 2-7 mm under the tubes). The tubes themselves are robust: medial-axis diameters are mostly 10-14 mm (16-20 mm where tubes merge), with necks of at least ~6 mm at the junctions.
findings.fix: Printing lens-up avoids support in these crevices, because the tunnels run roughly along x and print as vertical channels. They cannot be sanded. Either accept them as shadow lines or close them in Blender or Meshmixer before slicing if a clean painted surface matters more.

findings.title: No hollowing or splitting is needed
findings.evidence: Extents are 90.17 (x, lens axis) × 120.00 (y, width) × 84.73 (z, height) mm, which fits the 256 mm build volume in any orientation. A solid print would be 499 cm3 ≈ 620 g of PLA. With 3 walls, 15% sparse infill and 5 top layers, I estimate ~120-150 cm3 (~150-190 g including supports) and roughly 6-10 h on a P1S at 0.20 mm. This is a rough estimate; I did not slice the model. Splitting would only add a seam across the funnel-to-body blend, which would then need filling before the single paint colour.
findings.fix: Print in one piece and let the slicer's infill do the hollowing. Use 3-4 walls and 5-6 top layers so sanding does not break through on convex edges. Lightning or gyroid infill at 10-15% is fine.

results.summary: The print STL is ready to print. It is watertight with 0 boundary and 0 non-manifold edges, has one component (genus 7) and measures 90.2 × 120.0 × 84.7 mm with a volume of 499.4 cm3 (voxel cross-check 499.35, no odd-parity rays). It fits the P1S plate easily. Decimation and MeshFix lost no detail: compared with the GLB scaled the same way as print_stl.py, the maximum two-sided deviation is 0.115 mm and the 99.9th percentile is 0.022 mm, and the lens-axis cross-sections overlay exactly. The ≥30 mm lens requirement is met by the barrel (OD ≈ 39.5-40 mm, 12-14 mm long), the lip ring (≈ 37 mm) and the funnel (≈ 53 mm), but not by the glass (≈ 18 mm) or the bezel opening (≈ 27 mm), so the deliverable should state which part it means. Print it lens-up, standing on the viewfinder back, with build-plate-only tree supports and a brim; this keeps support out of the 2.3-3 mm lens groove and the tube tunnels, which would trap it if printed upright. Scratch outputs, including cross-section images such as /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-formnerd/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/scratchpad/verify/sect_zplane.png, are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-formnerd/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/scratchpad/verify/.

findings.title: The black hole is not a real void: the lens barrel fills the hood, so in one-colour paint the centre reads bright
findings.evidence: I checked this on the print STL with my own ray-cast front depth map. The lens axis is at y=65.2, z=32.35 mm, which matches the orchestrator. Depth from the frontmost point: the hood crown at r 23-28 sits about 3 mm back, the barrel lip at r 17-18 is 2.6 mm back and the barrel face 4.5 mm back. The glass (r<9) is only 9.4-10.4 mm deep. The only deep feature is a 2-2.5 mm wide groove at r 19.5-22 that is 16.7 mm deep. So there is no funnel: the barrel sits flush with the rim of a donut. I estimated how dark each area would look under soft studio light with one-colour paint (ambient-occlusion / heightfield AO, scale 0-1, where 1 is a fully open flat surface). The glass centre scores 0.86 and the barrel face 0.89, so both look almost as bright as the open body. Only the thin groove goes dark (0.13), and it reads as a lens-mount gap, not a hole. The clay renders confirm this: in clay_right and clay_front34 the centre is a light disc inside a soft bumper. The refinement steps asked for a knife-edge lip, glass about 15 mm deep and a 1.5-turn coil. None of these made it into g_to3d or the mesh, which is essentially c_gravity_well's 'rubber lens hood'.
findings.fix: In Blender (it is a Tripo mesh, so use booleans), work on the lens axis in STL coordinates: the axis runs along +X through y=65.2, z=32.35, and the hood front is at x≈90. First delete the existing barrel and glass (r<22, depth<17). Then subtract a revolved 'gravity well'. Keep the crown at r≥26.5. Profile as (radius, depth back from the hood front): (26.5, 2.5), (24, 4.5), (21, 8.5), (19, 12), (17, 16). The wall should steepen toward the axis. End it at ONE crisp edge, the event horizon, with only a 0.3 mm micro-chamfer. Behind that edge, cut a cylindrical throat r=17 down to 30-36 mm depth. Seat a new, plain lens at the bottom: a Ø32 glass disc with a single 1 mm step ring and no knurl. My estimate for this profile with the glass 36 mm deep: the glass centre drops from 0.86 to about 0.37 and the throat wall to about 0.22, while the funnel wall darkens steadily from about 0.8 at the crown to about 0.62 at the horizon edge. That is a valør pull made by form alone. To print it, split the hood/funnel off as an insert at the body front (x≈65), where the lens frame already gives a natural part line. Print the insert face-up with its axis vertical, so the void needs no internal supports. Glue it in and fill the seam before priming.

findings.title: Lens glass may not satisfy the hard 'Linse minimum 30 mm i diameter' requirement
findings.evidence: The brief (FormNerd Prosjektoversikt) says '01 Linse – Minimum 30 mm i diameter'. At 120 mm width, the flat glass measures about Ø18 (r<9), and with the retaining slope about Ø26 (r<13). Only the barrel (outer edge about Ø38-40) is over 30 mm. A strict jury reading 'linse' as the optical element would find it undersized.
findings.fix: Fold this into the funnel edit: make the dark glass disc Ø32 (r=16) inside the r=17 throat. That clearly meets the requirement and also enlarges the dark core. Note the Ø in the presentation. If the student keeps the current lens, grow the glass to r≥15 by removing the r 13-17 barrel face step.

findings.title: Concentric, static donut and perfectly balanced massing: nothing is being pulled
findings.evidence: I measured volume around the optical axis: 51.1% on the grip side and 48.9% on the far side, 46.9% below and 53.1% above. The centroid (y 63.0, z 35.4) sits almost on the lens axis. The grip and dial columns are parallel vertical pillars framing a symmetric torus hood. From the side (side_y0 ortho), the silhouette is a box (x 8-65) plus a cylinder (x 65-90), which is the conventional camera archetype with no tapering toward the lens. The hood lip is uniform within about 3 mm all the way round. The framework asks for deliberate visual imbalance and mass 'falling' toward one point. Here the holdning is neutral, and the hood reads as a bumper or 'photon ring' that sits rather than swallows. The one dynamic gesture is the braided tubes, but they run grip → dial/viewfinder, away from the void.
findings.fix: Apply these in order of cost. (a) Offset the throat axis from the hood-crown centre by 4-5 mm, down and toward the grip or toward where the tube enters. The funnel wall then becomes long and shallow on one side and steep on the other, so the rim looks dragged in. (b) Sweep the right-hand front tube, the one that runs from the top crossing down the right of the hood (y≈90-100), over the crown and ¾-1 turn down the funnel wall into the throat. Taper it from Ø10 to Ø4 and fuse it with R2-3 fillets. This links the top braid (disorder) to the void (swallowed). Keep its underside at 45° or more so the insert prints without supports. (c) Blend the body front into the hood with a large concave fillet (R15-20 between the body front at x≈65 and the hood outer at r≈29). The side silhouette then stretches into the lens instead of reading as box plus cylinder.

findings.title: No order-to-disorder gradient: the crisp blocks are stuck on, not deformed by the pull
findings.evidence: The viewfinder block (x 0-18, y 46-85, z 64-84) and the dial cylinder (around y 90-118) are untouched upright prisms on an all-soft bouba body with uniform radii. The organic-geometric contrast is a collage rather than a progression, so 'entropy' has no direction in the clay model. The judges' winner edits asked for both blocks to lean toward the lens, and the to3d prompt asked for it too. Neither the image nor the mesh has it.
findings.fix: Select each block's vertices above the body top line and shear or lean them 6-8° toward the lens axis, pivoting at their base. Optionally add 1 mm chamfers on the rear and back-facing edges of the blocks and the back slab (ordered, low-entropy zone), and leave everything near the hood soft. That makes a back-to-front order-to-disorder reading that survives one-colour paint.

findings.title: Viewfinder eyepiece faces sideways (windows on both side faces, blank rear face): wrong use semantics
findings.evidence: In side_y0 and side_y120 (my ortho views), there is an eyepiece window on BOTH side faces of the finder block, around x 3-15, z 70-80. The rear face (x=0) in the back ortho view is a blank flat tab, and the same shows in clay_front and tex_back34. This is a mirroring artefact from Tripo. A jury will read it as an eyepiece you look into from the side, perpendicular to the lens, which breaks the brukssemantikk of the camera archetype.
findings.fix: Fill both side windows (boolean union a box, then smooth). Cut one eyepiece on the rear face: a recess about 12 x 9 mm, 3 mm deep, with a 1 mm raised frame, centred on the block.

findings.title: USB-C appears twice, and both ports are too shallow to survive filler and paint
findings.evidence: Both end faces (grip end y=0 and dial end y=120) carry an identical stadium port at x≈25-29, z≈23-32. It shows in tex_back34 and in my side ortho views, and the two depth profiles match within 0.1 mm. At 0.1 mm sampling, the outer pill is about 3.5 x 8.6 mm but only about 0.7 mm deep, and the inner slot about 1.2 x 6 mm at about 1.8 mm deep. After primer, filler and paint this will look like a faint dimple. The duplicate is also a detailing error under criterion 8 (gruppering and sparse detailing).
findings.fix: Keep exactly one port: the grip-end port (y=0), which matches the hero render. Fill the y=120 port. Re-cut the kept one as a 3.3 x 9.0 mm stadium, 4 mm deep, with a 0.3 mm chamfer, so it holds a black shadow in one colour. Consider a 0.5 mm recessed inset panel around it, as in the hero.

findings.title: Fused-tube crevices and V-creases are Tripo artefacts that read as nonsense seams and cannot be finished
findings.evidence: Top-height profiles from my top ortho view show three problems. There is a slot about 2-2.5 mm wide and about 11-12 mm deep between the big top tube and the dial-side tube, around x≈45, y≈80 (z drops 72.6 → 61.1 → 72.7). There are V-valleys 2.5-3.5 mm deep between the parallel tubes around x≈30, y 60-90. There is a sharp V-crease about 5 mm deep where the tube merges into the grip, around x≈49, y≈40. These will trap primer and filler, cannot be sanded, and work against 'jevn modellfinish'. In clay, the fused tubes also read as plumbing, or as a hand clamped on top.
findings.fix: Use the Fill and Smooth sculpt brushes to turn every tube-to-tube and tube-to-body junction into a fillet of R≥3. Alternatively open the slot to at least 5 mm so a sanding stick fits. Make the dial knurl coarser (≥1 mm pitch) or smooth it, because a 0.3-0.5 mm knurl clogs under primer.

findings.title: Valør in the textured model pulls to the back, not the lens, and the hero no longer matches the 3D form
findings.evidence: Dark pixels (L<70) as a share of the object in each textured render: 37% front, 42% front34, 44% lens view, versus 66% back34 and 76% back. The camera is darkest from behind, because of the black back slab and the two black end panels. The CMF is a hard two-tone split, not the requested pearl-to-graphite gradient toward the funnel. Separately, the AI hero shows a shallow, protruding lens, so once the funnel edits are made the hero will contradict the physical model.
findings.fix: For the hero, re-render the edited model in Blender or KeyShot; no Tripo credits needed. Reserve the deep matte black for the funnel and throat only. Make the back slab and end panels mid graphite. Run a satin light-to-graphite gradient along the tubes toward the funnel. Check the render in greyscale so the darkest point is the throat.

results.summary: I checked the orchestrator's numbers: 120.0 x 90.2 x 84.7 mm, watertight, 0 non-manifold edges, 499.4 cm3, lens axis at y=65.2, z=32.4, and the radial profile all match. Those numbers also show the problem. The lens barrel sits flush with a soft donut hood, and the glass is only about 10 mm deep. Painted one colour, the centre stays almost as bright as the open body (about 0.86 on a 0-1 scale where 1 is a fully open flat surface). The clay model therefore reads as a friendly inflated camera with a rubber lens bumper, not as a void that light falls into. The massing is also perfectly balanced around the lens axis and static. Before printing, the student should, in priority order: cut a steepening funnel ending in one knife edge, with a Ø32 glass at 30-36 mm depth, printed as a face-up insert (this also secures the 30 mm lens requirement); offset the funnel and/or spiral a tube into it, and lean the two top blocks toward the lens; then fix the use-semantics errors (sideways eyepiece, duplicate shallow USB-C, crevices). Scratch analysis is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-formnerd/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/scratchpad/verify/ (ao_front.png, top.png, back.png, side_y0.png, side_y120.png, port_y0.png, synth.py).
